answers.quote: the Parliament passed its first important Act in 1773. called the Regulating Act to control the Company's Administration.
answers.notes: c01: Regulating Act 1773 was Parliament's first important Act.

answers.quote: the status of Governor of Bengal was raised to Governor General. His Council would consist of four members. The Governor General in Council was given the power to superintend and control the presidencies of Madras and Bombay in matters of war and peace.
answers.notes: c02: Council would consist of four members.

answers.quote: Pitt's India Act was passed in August, 1784. The purpose was to remove defects in the Regulating Act.
answers.notes: c05: Pitt's Act purpose was to remove defects in the Regulating Act.

answers.answer: ৬ জন কমিশনার, তাঁদের মধ্যে ২ জন ক্যাবিনেট মন্ত্রী
answers.quote: The Act established a Board of Control consisting of six commissioners, including, two Cabinet ministers. They were to control all matters of civil and military Government of the British territories in India.
answers.notes: c06: Board of Control of six commissioners including two Cabinet ministers.

answers.answer: গভর্নর-জেনারেল পরিষদের ঐক্যবদ্ধ বিরোধিতার মুখে পড়তেন এবং পরিষদকে অগ্রাহ্য করার ক্ষমতা তাঁর ছিল না
answers.quote: The Governor General had to face the opposition of his council, who united against him. He had no power to override them, though in case of an equal division he had a casting vote.
answers.notes: c04: GG faced united council opposition, no power to override, casting vote only on tie.

answers.quote: The Act clearly stated that the Presidencies of Madras and Bombay were to be subordinate to the Presidency of Bengal in all matters of war, diplomatic relations and revenue.
answers.notes: Statement 1 = c08 (Madras/Bombay subordinate in war, diplomacy, revenue); Statement 2 = c09 (1786 Act united GG and Commander-in-Chief). Both true.

answers.quote: The Company was deprived of its monopoly of trade with India. It was allowed to continue with its monopoly of trade with China for 20 years.
answers.notes: c12: Company deprived of India trade monopoly by Charter Act of 1813 (China monopoly kept).

answers.quote: Governor General of Bengal became the Governor General of India.
answers.notes: c14: By Act of 1833 GG of Bengal became GG of India.

answers.answer: ধর্ম, জন্মস্থান, বংশ বা বর্ণের কারণে কোনো ভারতীয় কোম্পানির চাকরি থেকে বঞ্চিত হবেন না
answers.quote: Section 87 of the Act declared, "that no native or natural born subject of the crown resident in India should be by reason only of his religion, place of birth, descent, colour or any of them be disqualified for any place in the company's service."
answers.notes: c16: Section 87 text on religion, place of birth, descent, colour.

answers.quote: The Council in its legislative capacity was to consist of 12 members. The "Legislative Councillors" were neatly distinguished from the "Executive Councillors" and by doing so, legislation was for the first time treated as a special function of the government requiring special machinery and special procedure.
answers.notes: c18: Council in legislative capacity to consist of 12 members.

answers.quote: The Act of 1793 thus laid the foundation of government by written laws and regulations in British India in place of the personal rule of the past rulers.
answers.notes: c11: Act of 1793 laid foundation of government by written laws and regulations.

answers.quote: the Parliament passed its first important Act in 1773. called the Regulating Act to control the Company's Administration.
answers.notes: Order from claims: Regulating Act 1773 (c01) < Pitt's Act Aug 1784 (c05) < Charter Act 1813 (c12) < Charter Act 1853 (c17/c18).

answers.quote: Warren Hastings (Governor-General from 1773 to 1785) was one of the many important figures who played a role in the expansion of Company power. The supreme head of the administration was the Governor-General. Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General, introduced several administrative reforms, notably in the sphere of justice.
answers.notes: c23: Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General (1773-1785).

answers.quote: The final wave of annexations occurred under Lord Dalhousie who was the Governor-General from 1848 to 1856. He devised a policy that came to be known as the Doctrine of Lapse.
answers.notes: c36: Dalhousie devised the Doctrine of Lapse.

answers.quote: The doctrine declared that if an Indian ruler died without a male heir his kingdom would "lapse", that is, become a part of Company territory. One kingdom after another was annexed simply by applying this doctrine: Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853) and Jhansi (1854).
answers.notes: c37 lists annexations in sequence starting Satara (1848), then Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853), Jhansi (1854).

answers.quote: Police, the third Pillar of the British administration was created by Cornwallis. This force was grouped into Thanas, headed by a Daroga who was an Indian.
answers.notes: c29: Police created by Cornwallis, thanas headed by Daroga.

answers.quote: Finally it was left to Bentinck, the Governor-General to legislate against Widow burning in December 1829.
answers.notes: c34: Bentinck legislated against sati in December 1829.

answers.answer: পরীক্ষা প্রতি বছর ইংল্যান্ডে অনুষ্ঠিত হত
answers.quote: The Charter Act of 1853 ultimately took away the power of the court of Directors to make nominations and made a provision for open competition. Subsequently the college at Hailybury was abolished in 1858 and the competitive examinations became the sole responsibility of the Civil Service Commission. This competitive examination was to be held annually in England and it was therefore, virtually impossible for an Indian to compete in it.
answers.notes: c33: examination held annually in England, virtually impossible for an Indian to compete.

answers.quote: Warren Hastings (Governor-General from 1773 to 1785) was one of the many important figures who played a role in the expansion of Company power. The supreme head of the administration was the Governor-General. Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General, introduced several administrative reforms, notably in the sphere of justice.
answers.notes: A Hastings=first GG/justice reforms (c23); B Cornwallis=police (c29); C Bentinck=sati abolition (c34); D Dalhousie=Doctrine of Lapse (c36).

answers.quote: Lord Stanley, President of the Board of Control introduced a bill for the 'Better Government' of India which became an Act of Parliament in August 1858. The Government of India passed from the hands of the English East India Company to the crown.
answers.notes: c20: Act of Aug 1858; government passed from Company to Crown.

answers.answer: বোর্ড অব কন্ট্রোল ও কোর্ট অব ডিরেক্টরস
answers.quote: The Board of control and court of Directors were abolished. Their place was taken by the Secretary of State of India and his India Council.
answers.notes: c21: Board of Control and Court of Directors abolished, replaced by Secretary of State and India Council.

answers.quote: In the centralized structure of power which was introduced in the provinces, all powers to govern India vested in the Secretary of State for India (and through him in the Crown). He was assisted by a fifteen-member council of ministers. In British India, the Secretary of State of India was assisted by the Viceroy, who was assisted by an executive council.
answers.notes: c68: Secretary of State assisted by a fifteen-member council; read with c21 (India Council took the place of Board/Court).

answers.answer: ১৮৫৮ থেকে গভর্নর-জেনারেলই ক্রাউনের প্রতিনিধি হিসেবে 'ভাইসরয়' নামে পরিচিত হন
answers.quote: The Governor General became known from now as the Viceroy or Crown's representative.
answers.notes: c22: GG became known from 1858 as Viceroy or Crown's representative; post not abolished.

answers.answer: A ও R দুটোই সঠিক এবং R হল A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: In the centralized structure of power which was introduced in the provinces, all powers to govern India vested in the Secretary of State for India (and through him in the Crown). He was assisted by a fifteen-member council of ministers. In British India, the Secretary of State of India was assisted by the Viceroy, who was assisted by an executive council.
answers.notes: Core covered: c20 (1858 transfer to Crown) + c68 (all powers vested in Secretary of State for India). Partial gap: no claim explicitly states the Secretary of State was a British Cabinet member, so R's cabinet detail is not verbatim-covered by claims; vesting itself fully explains A.

answers.quote: The Arms Act was passed in 1878, disallowing Indians from possessing arms. In the same year, the Vernacular Press Act was also enacted in an effort to silence those who were critical of the government.
answers.notes: c43: Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act both passed in 1878.

answers.quote: Lord Lytton was succeeded by Lord Ripon in 1880. He repealed the Vernacular Press Act, promoted local self-government institutions, encouraged the spread of education and brought the Afghan War to an end.
answers.notes: c48: Ripon (succeeded Lytton 1880) repealed the Vernacular Press Act.

answers.quote: During his period the maximum age for appearing in the Indian Civil Service examination was reduced from 21 to 19 years.
answers.notes: c46: under Lytton max ICS age reduced from 21 to 19 years.

answers.answer: ব্রিটিশ বা ইউরোপীয় ব্যক্তিদের বিচার ভারতীয় বিচারকরাও করতে পারবেন
answers.quote: In 1883, there was a furore over the attempt by the government to introduce the Ilbert Bill. The bill provided for the trial of British or European persons by Indians, and sought equality between British and Indian judges in the country. But when white opposition forced the government to withdraw the bill, Indians were enraged.
answers.notes: c45: Ilbert Bill provided for trial of British/European persons by Indians, equality of judges.

answers.quote: In 1905, Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal. The British argued for dividing Bengal for reasons of administrative convenience. Even so, instead of removing the non-Bengali areas from the province, the government separated East Bengal and merged it with Assam.
answers.notes: c50: In 1905 Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal.

answers.answer: প্রথম নির্বাচিত অ-সরকারি সদস্যদের প্রতিনিধিত্ব এবং মুসলিম সম্প্রদায়ের পৃথক প্রতিনিধিত্ব
answers.quote: The scope of political institutions in the provinces was expanded a little further following the introduction of Council of India Act, 1909. This Act introduced for the first time a "representative element" in British India, which included elected non-official members. This Act also introduced separate representation to Muslim community.
answers.notes: c53: 1909 Act introduced representative element with elected non-official members + separate representation for Muslim community.

answers.quote: In 1905, Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal. The British argued for dividing Bengal for reasons of administrative convenience. Even so, instead of removing the non-Bengali areas from the province, the government separated East Bengal and merged it with Assam.
answers.notes: Pair 3 is wrong: partition was by Curzon in 1905 (c50), while Ripon repealed the VPA (c48). Pairs 1 (c52), 2 (c43/c47), 4 (c50) are correct.

answers.quote: The Government of India Act 1919 devolved some authority to the provincial governments, retaining the control of the central government (unitary government) on them. It divided the subjects for jurisdiction of administration and sources of revenue between centre and provinces. The provincial subjects were divided into "transferred" and "reserved" categories.
answers.notes: c54: 1919 Act divided provincial subjects into transferred and reserved categories (dyarchy).

answers.quote: In 1919, Gandhiji gave a call for a satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act that the British had just passed. The Act curbed fundamental rights such as the freedom of expression and strengthened police powers.
answers.notes: c55: Rowlatt Act (1919); Gandhi's satyagraha call in 1919.

answers.answer: কমিশনে কোনো ভারতীয় প্রতিনিধি ছিল না
answers.quote: In 1927, the British government in England decided to send a commission headed by Lord Simon to decide India's political future. The Commission had no Indian representative. The decision created an outrage in India. All political groups decided to boycott the Commission.
answers.notes: c56: Simon Commission had no Indian representative; all groups boycotted.

answers.quote: The first attempt by Indians themselves to prepare a Constitution of India was made in the Nehru Report (1928). The Nehru Report was known as such because it was named after the chairman of its drafting committee, Motilal Nehru.
answers.notes: c57: Nehru Report named after drafting committee chairman Motilal Nehru.

answers.answer: দেশীয় রাজাদের মধ্যে যুক্তরাষ্ট্রে যোগদান নিয়ে ঐকমত্য ছিল না
answers.quote: the federal government could not be formed because there was no unanimity among the princes to join the federation. And election to the provincial legislature as per the Government of India Act, 1935 was held in 1937. Following the election of 1937, provincial governments headed by the Indian National Congress were formed in eight provinces.
answers.notes: c60: federation could not be formed for want of unanimity among princes to join.

answers.answer: তিনটি তালিকা: যুক্তরাষ্ট্রীয়, যুগ্ম ও প্রাদেশিক; সঙ্গে যুক্তরাষ্ট্রীয় আদালত
answers.quote: This Act also provided for three lists of divisions of power between the federation (central government) and provinces: federal (central), concurrent and provincial. The Act also provided for establishment of a federal court to adjudicate disputes between federation and provinces.
answers.notes: c59: three lists (federal, concurrent, provincial) + federal court.

answers.quote: The Government of India Act 1919 devolved some authority to the provincial governments, retaining the control of the central government (unitary government) on them. It divided the subjects for jurisdiction of administration and sources of revenue between centre and provinces. The provincial subjects were divided into "transferred" and "reserved" categories.
answers.notes: Statement 1 = c54 (1919 transferred/reserved); Statement 2 = c58 (1935 provincial autonomy). Both true.

answers.quote: It consisted of three cabinet members - Lord Pathic-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and Mr. A.V. Alexander. It, however, made its own proposal which was announced simultaneously on 16 May, 1946 in England as well as in India.
answers.notes: c63: Cabinet Mission of three cabinet members, proposals announced 16 May 1946. 1942/3 distractor is Cripps (c62, single cabinet member, 1942).

answers.quote: C. Rajagopalachari, popularly known as Rajaji, served as member of the Interim Government of 1946 and as free India's first Indian Governor-General.
answers.notes: c67: Rajagopalachari was free India's first Indian Governor-General.

answers.quote: when the Constituent Assembly first met on December 9, 1946, it was boycotted by the Muslim League, and it functioned without the participation of the Muslim League.
answers.notes: c64: Constituent Assembly first met 9 Dec 1946, boycotted by Muslim League.

answers.quote: It consisted of three cabinet members - Lord Pathic-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and Mr. A.V. Alexander. It, however, made its own proposal which was announced simultaneously on 16 May, 1946 in England as well as in India.
